transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me. As you know, we're preparing to launch an eighth-grade makerspace program for the spring semester, and before I give final authorization, I'd like to gather input from each of you based on your areas of expertise. The draft proposal calls for 24 students supervised by one STEM teacher, meeting twice a week, with soldering stations, hand tools, a laser cutter, standard metal components, and cloud-based CAD files. I'd like to go around and hear any concerns or recommendations each of you has regarding implementation. Let's start with you — what should I know before approving this?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to flag an important safety issue. I just completed my room-safety review this week, and it found that the makerspace may enroll no more than 16 students — not 24 as the draft currently shows. Additionally, any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults. The draft program form still shows the original staffing and enrollment numbers, so these limits haven't been reflected yet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to raise a health concern from my review of the participating students' health records. I found one student with a documented severe nickel allergy. That student may participate only when the program uses nickel-free components, and I must approve the materials list before each session. I should also note that this health-record review has not yet been added to the program file, so it needs to be documented there. Given that the draft proposal specifies 'standard metal components,' we'll need to address this before approval.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to raise a technology compliance issue. I confirmed with the district technology office that student design files for this equipment may not use cloud storage. The approved workflow requires an offline design workstation with files transferred by encrypted USB after an IT malware scan. However, the draft program still contains the cloud-storage instruction, and I have not yet replaced it. This needs to be corrected before approval.
